newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - March 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Hong Kong government's blueprint for public spending in the fiscal year 1997/98, which topped HK$200 billion for the first time, dominated coverage.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL - Quoting sources, the newspaper said a surplus of HK$25 billion would be revealed in the 1996/97 budget. The financial budget for 1997/98 would continue to show considerable surplus.

-- MING PAO - The government had a surplus of more than HK$10 billion and political parties were considering putting pressure on the govennment to reduce taxes and use the huge amount of financial surplus on social welfare.

-- SING TAO - An emergency proposal has been put forward at the National People's Congress (NPC) meeting in Beijing to bar Hong Kong people with right of abode elsewhere from seeking election to the NPC in 1998.
-- WEN WEI PO - A newly-proposed National Defence Law would include provisions aimed at curbing activities which advocate Taiwan's independence and the splitting up of China.
-- A methodology has been drafted to elect Hong Kong representatives to the National People's Congress. The formula would be ready before January 1998.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission is investigating suspected manipulators of the stock market.
- China's long-awaited Securities Law would be passed in 1997.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Top employees in the office of Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa have been told they will not lose their jobs when top civil servants are seconded to the office.
